title: Auxiliary Power Unit — Description and Ground Operating Envelope

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew description of the auxiliary power unit, what it can supply on the ground and in flight, and how the crew should manage it on a hot turnaround when bleed and electrical demand compete.

sections.purpose: This entry describes the auxiliary power unit to the flight crew, what it supplies on the ground and in flight, and how it behaves when the ramp is hot and the demand is high.
sections.description: The auxiliary power unit provides electrical power and bleed air on the ground and can be used in flight within the published envelope. On the ground it is normally the source for air conditioning during boarding and for the engine start. The unit protects itself: if it reaches an internal limit it will shut down and it will not restart until it has cooled, and there is no crew action that will override that. This behaviour is most likely on a hot ramp, late in a day of short sectors, and with the bleed and a heavy electrical load selected together. It is not a failure and it does not need a technical log entry unless it happens repeatedly. Crews reporting it should record the outside air temperature and how many sectors the aircraft has flown that day, because those two facts are what the engineering assessment depends on and they are almost never written down. On aircraft at the later control standard the ground operating envelope is wider and the shutdown is much less likely.
sections.crew_procedure: On a hot turnaround, select the bleed for air conditioning first and add the electrical load progressively rather than together. If ground air is available, use it and leave the unit on electrical load only. After an automatic shutdown, do not attempt an immediate restart; allow the cooling period before selecting the master switch on again. Record the outside air temperature and the sector count in the technical log entry if the shutdown is reported.

type_data.crew_action: Manage bleed and electrical demand progressively on a hot ramp. Allow the cooling period after an automatic shutdown.
